profile_text.body:
iNaturalist is a social network for naturalists, according to the site, where people record observations of plants and animals, share them with friends and researchers, and learn about the natural world. Users open the app and photograph any wild plant, animal, fungi, or other organism from their neighborhood or anywhere in the world. Observations are open and freely available to researchers, conservation practitioners, and curious individuals, and when the community agrees on an identification, an observation becomes "research grade" and enters the global scientific record. The site describes the platform as a tool that connects people, nature, and knowledge, and says it works on desktop at iNaturalist.org and through mobile apps.

The company is the California Academy of Sciences and National Geographic Society, and its tracked product is iNaturalist, listed under Education and Research AI. The product note describes AI species suggestions. It is free, and its stated audience is students 13 and older, or younger with parent permission, along with teachers. The note describes consumer terms with no school agreement, most content public by default, and a parental permission process for users 12 and under.

The site highlights examples of the platform's use: a Frosted Phoenix moth not spotted in decades, found by a tourist in New Zealand; Inimia nat, abbreviated I. nat, a new-to-science mantis species found by a woman in Australia walking in her neighborhood; and local volunteers in California who came together through iNaturalist to protect migrating amphibians crossing a busy road.
